# Harness Engineering Research

> An MCP server that turns a non-technical founder's plain-language product request into real,
> verified local infrastructure on Floci, plus a research reference on harness engineering as a
> discipline (Agent = Model + Harness).

This repo has two parts. The first is a working demo harness: an MCP server (`harness/`) that
matches a plain-language request against a capability catalog (`catalog/`), executes real
provisioning steps, and independently re-verifies the result against live infrastructure before
ever claiming success — no LLM self-report is trusted. The second is a curated research
reference on harness engineering (system prompts, tools/skills/MCP, sandboxing, orchestration,
memory) as a discipline distinct from model choice.

## Docs

- [README.md](README.md): entry point, split into founder / engineer / AI-agent sections.
- [harness/README.md](harness/README.md): the MCP server's architecture, tools, and how to run it.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): how an AI coding agent connects to and calls this MCP server.
- [tasks/README.md](tasks/README.md): benchmark results (before/after numbers, including honest
  negative findings) from measuring the harness against a fixed scoring task set.
- [research/research-links.md](research/research-links.md): curated harness-engineering research link pack.
- [VOCAB.md](research/VOCAB.md): shared harness-engineering vocabulary.

## Design decisions

- [research/agdr/AgDR-0001-shared-backend-naming-scope-isolation.md](research/agdr/AgDR-0001-shared-backend-naming-scope-isolation.md):
  isolating multiple agents on one shared backend via naming scope, not per-agent infrastructure.
- [research/agdr/AgDR-0002-flock-based-state-locking.md](research/agdr/AgDR-0002-flock-based-state-locking.md):
  cross-process state locking for an MCP server where every client spawns its own subprocess.

## Optional

- [research/history/GAME_PLAN.md](research/history/GAME_PLAN.md): archived design rationale from the
  project's original build.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): how to set up, test, and contribute to this repo.
